subject: Post-call: Residency priorities, pinning, and follow-ups
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Joanna Hunt <joanna.hunt@luminaryhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Residency priorities, pinning, and follow-ups

Hi Joanna — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps while items are fresh:

Summary of what I heard
- Primary need: keep patient-identifiable input and inference logs within EU region(s) for regulatory/compliance reasons.
- Secondary: require clear failover behavior (APAC/US only as warm standby, no active replication of PII) and point-in-time backup policies.
- Auditability: need fine-grained request/response logging for tracing, but with redaction/PII controls and retention options.

Proposed immediate asks (can we confirm these by EOD Tuesday?):
1) Residency pinning: confirm that you want (a) single-region EU pin (primary) with manual failover, or (b) active-active across EU regions. From our discussion it sounded like (a).
2) Retention baseline: confirm target retention for logs/inference results (30/90/365 days) so we can map to our retention profiles.
3) Encryption/KMS: confirm whether Luminary will supply a customer-managed key (BYOK) or use Redwood-managed KMS for backups.

What I can send next (attached)
- Redwood residency whitepaper (high level) — explains pinning, failover, and backup semantics.
- Data-retention matrix (spreadsheet) — maps retention windows to cost and export options.

If that aligns, I recommend a 30-minute follow-up with Marissa (technical lead) to validate the exact pinning config and answer any SOC/controls questions. Proposed slots: Wed 9/15 10:00–10:30 PT or Thu 9/16 16:00–16:30 PT.

Thanks — looking forward to locking these down.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood_residency_whitepaper.pdf (PDF), data_retention_matrix.xlsx (XLSX)

From: Joanna Hunt <joanna.hunt@luminaryhealth.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: Luminary Health Security Team <security@luminaryhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Residency priorities, pinning, and follow-ups

Thanks, Nikhil — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Residency pinning: yes, option (a) — single-region EU pin with manual failover. We are uncomfortable with any automatic cross-region replication of PII.
- Retention: default logs should be kept 90 days. Inference outputs that include PII should be purgeable per-case; we'll provide a list of classes we consider PII.
- Backups: backups must be encrypted with our KMS (we can provide a key). We also need backup retention policy up to 365 days for disaster recovery, but access to backups should be restricted.

Open questions for Redwood (can Marissa cover these?):
1) When manual failover is triggered, how long before routing resumes to the new region? Is there an RTO estimate?
2) Are backups stored in the pinned region only, or are there multi-region backup copies? We prefer single-region storage unless required for compliance.
3) Logging redaction: can Redwood suppress or mask specific fields at ingestion and still preserve trace ids for debugging?

We can do Wed 9/15 10:00 PT for the technical call. Please send a calendar invite.

—Joanna
Joanna Hunt
CTO, Luminary Health
joanna.hunt@luminaryhealth.com

(On the Security Team side, I'll loop security@luminaryhealth.com in the next thread.)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Joanna Hunt <joanna.hunt@luminaryhealth.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call: Residency priorities, pinning, and follow-ups

Hi Joanna — thanks, and great questions. High-level answers below; we can use the Wed slot to walk the detailed diagrams.

1) Failover/RTO
- Manual failover: typically 3–8 minutes to cut traffic and warm caches depending on model KV sizes; complete recovery time to full throughput can be 15–45 minutes for large sequence workloads.
- We provide a canary test before full cutover and a rollback path. We document the exact steps in the runbook we'll share during the call.

2) Backups
- By default, backups are stored in the pinned region only. Multi-region backup copies are optional and require explicit enablement (and appropriate contractual approvals).
- Backups are encrypted at rest using AES-256; when you provide a customer-managed key (BYOK), snapshots are encrypted with your key.

3) Logging & redaction
- We support request-level redaction filters at ingestion: you can define field-level rules (JSON paths) to mask or drop fields before they are persisted.
- Traceability: redaction preserves non-identifying metadata (trace ids, request ids, timestamps) so debugging remains possible. Full request content can be exported under access controls if needed for audits.

Other notes
- Retention mapping: our standard template supports 30/90/365 day profiles. For inference outputs flagged as PII we support TTL-based purge and on-demand delete APIs.
- Access controls: audit logs + KMS access policies are surfaced in the Console; we also support SIEM forwarding for audit retention.

Attached: updated data_retention_matrix.xlsx (I've added a column showing cost delta for BYOK-enabled backups).

I'll be on the Wed 9/15 10:00 PT call; joining details to follow from Nikhil.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: data_retention_matrix.xlsx

Date: 2026-09-14T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Residency priorities, pinning, and follow-ups

Joanna — quick note on backups and encryption controls to confirm alignment:
- BYOK flow: Luminary uploads a key to your preferred KMS (e.g., AWS KMS or GCP KMS) and grants Redwood encryption-only access. Redwood never has the plaintext key.
- Backup immutability: we can configure retention locks at the storage layer to prevent accidental purge for the agreed DR window.
- Export controls: exports of data for debugging are gated by RBAC + approval workflow; we log every export event.

If your security team wants a short artifacts pack (SAML configs, KMS flow diagram, sample audit entries) I'll prepare that post-call.

—Ben

- Ben: if you can produce the KMS flow diagram and a sample audit log entry before the meeting, that would be great.
